title: Level 13: I2C Master — Reading an MPU-6050 Accelerometer/Gyroscope
aim: To configure the ATmega328P's TWI (Two-Wire Interface, I2C compatible) as a master and communicate with an MPU-6050 6-axis IMU sensor at address 0x68, reading accelerometer and gyroscope raw data via register access.
objective: Understand the I2C bus protocol (START, address, ACK, data, STOP conditions), the ATmega328P TWI register set (TWCR, TWSR, TWDR, TWBR), 7-bit addressing, the two-phase read transaction (write address + register, then read data), and MPU-6050 register map.
theory:
I2C — Inter-Integrated Circuit Protocol

I2C (pronounced 'I-squared-C') is a synchronous, half-duplex, multi-master, multi-slave serial protocol using only 2 wires:

  • SCL (Serial Clock Line) — Master-generated clock
  • SDA (Serial Data Line) — Bidirectional data

Both lines are open-drain with pull-up resistors (typically 4.7 kΩ to VCC). Any device can pull a line LOW; pull-ups hold it HIGH when no device drives it. This allows multiple masters and multiple slaves on the same two wires, with bus arbitration.

7-Bit Addressing

Each I2C slave has a unique 7-bit address (from 16 defined by manufacturer + user-configurable bits). The master addresses a specific slave by sending its 7-bit address followed by a direction bit:

  • address << 1 | 0 = Write (SLA+W)
  • address << 1 | 1 = Read (SLA+R)

The MPU-6050 has address 0x68 (AD0 pin tied to GND) or 0x69 (AD0 tied to VCC).

I2C Transaction Anatomy

Every I2C transaction follows this protocol: START → [Address+W/R] → [ACK] → [Data bytes with ACKs] → STOP

A START condition is a high-to-low transition on SDA while SCL is HIGH. A STOP condition is a low-to-high transition on SDA while SCL is HIGH. These are the only times SDA changes while SCL is HIGH — during data bits, SDA must be stable when SCL is HIGH.

Every byte must be acknowledged by the receiver pulling SDA LOW on the 9th clock (ACK). If not acknowledged (NACK), the transaction is aborted.

Reading an MPU-6050 Register (2-Phase Transaction)

To read a register from a slave:
Phase 1: START → SLA+W → Register address → STOP (or REPEATED_START)
Phase 2: START → SLA+R → Read data byte → NACK → STOP

ATmega328P TWI Registers

  • TWBR — Bit Rate Register. SCL frequency = F_CPU / (16 + 2 × TWBR × prescaler). For 100 kHz at 16 MHz: TWBR = 72.
  • TWCR — Control Register. Key bits: TWINT (interrupt flag — write 1 to clear and proceed), TWSTA (generate START), TWSTO (generate STOP), TWEN (enable TWI), TWEA (send ACK).
  • TWSR — Status Register. Upper 5 bits = TWI status code. Read after each step to confirm ACK received, data ready, etc.
  • TWDR — Data Register. Load with byte to send, or read received byte from here.

MPU-6050 Key Registers

  • 0x6B (PWR_MGMT_1) — Write 0x00 to wake device from sleep
  • 0x3B–0x40 — Accelerometer X,Y,Z High/Low bytes (16-bit each)
  • 0x43–0x48 — Gyroscope X,Y,Z High/Low bytes (16-bit each)
  • 0x75 (WHO_AM_I) — Returns 0x68, confirms identity

I2C Pull-Up Resistors

SCL and SDA require pull-up resistors to VCC. The value affects rise time and maximum speed: 4.7 kΩ for 100 kHz (standard), 2.2 kΩ for 400 kHz (fast mode). The ATmega328P has internal pull-ups (~50 kΩ) — too weak for reliable I2C; always use external resistors.

pretest.question: How many wires does I2C use?
pretest.explanation: I2C uses exactly 2 wires: SCL (clock) and SDA (data). Both are open-drain with pull-up resistors to VCC.

pretest.question: What is the MPU-6050 I2C address when AD0 is tied to GND?
pretest.explanation: The MPU-6050 defaults to I2C address 0x68 when the AD0 pin is grounded. Connecting AD0 to VCC shifts it to 0x69 — allowing two MPU-6050s on one bus.

pretest.question: What does START condition mean in I2C?
options: SCL falls while SDA is LOW
SDA falls from HIGH to LOW while SCL remains HIGH
SDA rises while SCL is LOW
pretest.explanation: A START condition is defined as SDA transitioning HIGH→LOW while SCL is HIGH. This is the only legal SDA change while SCL is HIGH (during data, SDA must be stable).

pretest.question: What does TWINT flag in TWCR indicate?
options: TWI operation complete — write 1 to TWINT to clear it and proceed to next step
pretest.explanation: TWINT is set by hardware when a TWI operation completes (START sent, byte transmitted, ACK received, etc.). Software clears it by writing 1 to TWINT, which starts the next TWI operation.

pretest.question: For I2C 100 kHz at 16 MHz with no prescaler, what TWBR value is needed?
What is a REPEATED_START (Sr) in I2C?
options: A START condition without preceding STOP — retains bus ownership for multi-phase transactions
pretest.explanation: A Repeated START allows the master to change transfer direction (write→read) or address a different slave without releasing the bus. Used in the two-phase read transaction.

pretest.question: What does ACK (Acknowledge) in I2C mean?
options: Receiver pulls SDA LOW during the 9th clock (confirming byte received)
pretest.explanation: After each transmitted byte, the receiver must acknowledge by pulling SDA LOW during the 9th SCL pulse. NACK (SDA remains HIGH) indicates the receiver cannot accept more data.

pretest.question: Which MPU-6050 register must be written 0x00 to exit sleep mode?
pretest.explanation: The MPU-6050 boots in sleep mode. Writing 0x00 to register 0x6B (PWR_MGMT_1) clears the SLEEP bit, waking the device and enabling sensor data output.

pretest.question: Why are external pull-up resistors required on I2C lines?
options: I2C lines are open-drain — they can only be pulled LOW, requiring external pull-ups to define the HIGH state
pretest.explanation: Open-drain outputs can only sink current (pull LOW). The pull-up resistor provides the path to VCC for the HIGH logic level. Internal 50 kΩ pull-ups are too weak for reliable I2C above a few kHz.

pretest.question: What 16-bit accelerometer value represents 1g in MPU-6050 default ±2g range?
pretest.explanation: In ±2g range, the sensitivity is 16384 LSB/g. So raw value 16384 = 1g, 32767 ≈ 2g. Divide raw values by 16384.0 to get acceleration in g.

procedure: Include #include <avr/io.h> and #include <util/delay.h>. Wire: SDA → Arduino A4 (PC4), SCL → Arduino A5 (PC5). Add external 4.7 kΩ pull-up resistors from SDA and SCL to 3.3V or 5V (match MPU-6050's VLOGIC). Power MPU-6050 from 3.3V.
Configure I2C: Set TWSR prescaler to 1 (TWPS = 0x00), then compute and load TWBR for 100 kHz: TWSR = 0x00; TWBR = 72;

Write TWI helper functions: twi_start() (set TWSTA|TWEN|TWINT and wait for TWINT), twi_stop() (set TWSTO|TWEN|TWINT), twi_write(byte) (load TWDR, set TWEN|TWINT, wait), twi_read_ack() and twi_read_nack() for reading with or without ACK.
Wake the MPU-6050: call twi_start(), write SLA+W (0x68<<1|0 = 0xD0), write register 0x6B, write data 0x00, call twi_stop().
Implement a function to read a register: twi_start() → write SLA+W(0xD0) → write register_addr → twi_start() (repeated) → write SLA+R(0xD1) → twi_read_nack() → twi_stop(). Return TWDR.
Read the WHO_AM_I register (0x75) — should return 0x68 to confirm device identity before reading sensors.

Read 6 bytes starting at ACCEL_XOUT_H (0x3B) by doing a repeated read: start at register 0x3B, then read 6 consecutive bytes with ACKs, last byte with NACK. Combine High+Low bytes: int16_t ax = (TWDR_H << 8) | TWDR_L; for each axis.
Convert raw values to g: float ax_g = ax / 16384.0;. Transmit values over UART (from Exp 10) to monitor on a terminal. Tilt the sensor and observe axis values change.

posttest.question: What TWI status code appears in TWSR after a successful START condition?
posttest.explanation: After generating a START condition, TWSR (masked with 0xF8) returns 0x08 (START transmitted). After REPEATED_START, it returns 0x10.

posttest.question: What happens if no slave ACKs the master's address byte?
options: TWSR returns NACK status (0x20 for SLA+W) — firmware must abort with STOP
posttest.explanation: If no slave ACKs, SDA remains HIGH on the 9th clock. TWSR shows 0x20 (SLA+W NACK) or 0x48 (SLA+R NACK). The firmware should STOP and retry or handle the error.

posttest.question: I2C maximum speed in standard mode is 100 kHz. What speed does Fast Mode support?
posttest.explanation: Fast Mode I2C supports up to 400 kHz. Fast Mode Plus (FM+) reaches 1 MHz, and High-Speed Mode (HS) reaches 3.4 MHz.

posttest.question: What is the advantage of SPI over I2C for high-bandwidth data transfer?
options: SPI is full-duplex and can run at 10+ MHz vs I2C's 400 kHz max in fast mode
posttest.explanation: SPI can run at tens of MHz without complex acknowledge mechanisms. I2C tops out at ~3.4 MHz and requires ACK handshake each byte. SPI is preferred for SD cards, displays, and ADCs.

posttest.question: The gyroscope in MPU-6050 measures:
options: Angular rate in degrees per second (°/s)
posttest.explanation: The MPU-6050 gyroscope measures angular rate (how fast it's rotating) in °/s. The default full-scale is ±250 °/s. Integrate over time to get angle.

posttest.question: What is a watchdog timer used for?
posttest.explanation: WDT auto-resets MCU when not periodically cleared.

posttest.question: Which is NOT a valid ATmega328P port?
posttest.explanation: ATmega328P has Port B, C, and D only.

posttest.question: What happens to SRAM when power is removed?
In an ISR, interrupts are automatically:
posttest.explanation: AVR clears the I-bit in SREG on ISR entry.

posttest.question: What does the SREG register contain?
posttest.explanation: SREG is the Status Register holding CPU arithmetic flags and the global interrupt enable (I-bit).

feedback: Superb! I2C is ubiquitous in modern electronics — temperature sensors, OLED displays, real-time clocks, IMUs, and EEPROM chips all use I2C. You now understand the full TWI protocol at the register level, enabling you to interface any I2C device.
